BiblicalUsage: Shabbathon is a deeper rest than the ordinary Sabbath, a solemn rest laid on the Day of Atonement and on the land in its seventh year. Where the weekly Sabbath stops the work of hands, the shabbathon stops the work of the whole year, letting the land lie fallow and the people afflict their souls before God. The word is used only of these set-apart rests, never of a common holiday.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God built deep rest into the rhythm of His people, not as a luxury but as a command. The shabbathon tells me that rest is holy when God appoints it, and that the land itself belongs to Him.
